_comment: MSTR capital structure: claims ranking ahead of common stock. Consumed by
Updated 2026-08-24: cash $4.80B -> $6.67B (USD Reserve +$300M, new USD Cash
account +$1.57B, both funded by the ATM raise). Preferred $15.50B -> $15.36B
after a $136.4M STRC repurchase - the first real step toward STRC trading back
at its $100 stated amount, which management said gates any dividend cut.
Converts unchanged and still far out of the money.
pricemodel/valuation.py for net NAV, net mNAV and structural leverage. The daily
email report does not read this file - its mNAV is gross by design.
SOURCING: real figures from public reporting, current to 2026-08-22, but not read
out of a filing directly - so 'verified' stays false and every net-NAV figure is
labelled accordingly. Confirm against the latest 10-Q before quoting.
Convertible notes: $6.7B aggregate principal outstanding as of 2026-05-25, after
the $1.5B repurchase of the 2029 notes completed that month. The per-series
split below is approximate; what matters for the valuation is that every series
strikes in the hundreds of dollars while MSTR trades near $119, so all of it is
far out of the money and counts as debt with no dilution. The conclusion is
robust to the exact strikes - it would take a multi-fold rally to change it.
Preferred: $15.5B aggregate notional as of 2026-05-25 across the STRK/STRF/STRD/
STRC series. STRK is the only convertible one, at 0.1 MSTR shares per share -
also deeply out of the money here. annual_dividend_usd is an ESTIMATE: roughly
10% blended across the stack, since STRF and STRD both carry 10% perpetual
non-cumulative dividends. It is reported as a recurring drain on the treasury,
never subtracted from NAV, so an approximation here cannot corrupt net NAV.
cash_usd: the $4.8B USD reserve reported 2026-08-17.
other_assets_usd: 0 - the software business is small and not independently valued
here. Leaving it at zero understates net NAV slightly, which is the safe side.
